findings.title: GPU benchmark does not time the production held-fold evaluator (different cache cast path)
findings.claim: The GPU gate prices every held evaluation with the p95 of benchmark._eval_model, but production selection scores with workflow._score_model -> data.view_inputs. These are two different paths for loading and casting the cache, and the production one costs more on the host. P §9 asks for a benchmark run «con stessi loader/file placement, cache cast, flag numerici ... dei fit».
findings.evidence: Benchmark: benchmark.py:155 `x = dataset.features[start:stop].to(device=device, dtype=torch.float32)` (torch cast of a preloaded FP16 TensorTrainingSet). Production: workflow.py:241 `x = torch.from_numpy(D.view_inputs(bundle.cache, depth, rows)).to(device)`. Per 32-window batch, data.py:130-136 runs lengths_for() over the whole cache, FP16 `np.isfinite(features[available])`, and `np.where(...).astype(np.float32)`. Gate: resources.py:155 `raw += MAX_LRS * (MAX_EPOCHS*c["train"] + MAX_EVALS*c["eval"] ...` with MAX_EVALS=304 per trajectory; requested walltime = 2*raw (resources.py:93). I reproduced this on a Mac fixture with production geometry (1907 windows, 160x384 FP16, 40 users, 953 held windows; model forward excluded, identical in both) using scratch scripts eval_overhead.py and eval_breakdown.py under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-simonebenatti-dev-wearusfm/d9aa6af4-72b7-4d2a-8229-4444e8ca2c8f/scratchpad/poseheads/agents/lens1/. Output: `production _score_model host work: median 330.8 ms per held-fold evaluation (953 windows)` vs `benchmark _eval_model host work: median 146.4 ms`. Breakdown: `prod view_inputs 164.2 ms` vs `bench cast 22.8 ms`; selection_statistics is about the same in both (142.6 vs 160.5 ms). Inside view_inputs, per batch: isfinite on FP16 2.09 ms, np.where 0.81 ms, astype 0.43 ms. Model values are unaffected: FP16->FP32 is exact and padded positions are zero in both paths.
findings.failure_scenario: The benchmark measures eval about 1.7-2.3x too low on the host side (Mac numbers; Ice Lake numpy FP16 loops may differ). In the worst case with all extensions (6 LR x 300 epochs, 40,128 held evaluations), this unmeasured systematic excess uses up part of the factor-2 walltime margin. If eval is a large share of per-epoch time, a selection/control job could exceed its requested walltime: TIMEOUT, technical_failure, the GPU hours already used are lost and the phase stops. No scientific value changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) time workflow._score_model in benchmark_gpu, on a FoldBundle built from the train cache, so eval_seconds measures the fit code path; or (b) have _score_model and _predict_locked read held rows through the same FP16 TensorTrainingSet/torch per-batch cast used in training and in the benchmark, and compute lengths once. (b) gives bitwise-identical inputs. Do this before the benchmark job runs.

findings.title: Initial-state hashes are computed before each trajectory but not persisted before the first fit
findings.claim: J new_head_common.module_rng_policy says «save init state hashes per head/seed/fold before first fit». The code computes Trajectory.initial_sha256 at creation (train.py:232) and checks it is the same across LRs (train.py:547-550). It only writes it into the final selection report (train.py:563) and the refit manifest (workflow.py:404), both saved when the stage completes.

findings.failure_scenario: If a selection, control or refit job hits technical_failure mid-search (NaN, OOM, determinism error, TIMEOUT), its receipt and log hold no initial-state hash. Diagnosis must rebuild the hash from the seed. No effect on results: the init is deterministic and every in-memory state carries the hash.
findings.suggested_fix: In _run_search/_run_refits, print one JSON event (head, lr, fold/seed, initial_sha256) right after the trajectories are created and before train_to_step. This is logging only, with no numerical effect. Alternatively, amend the J/P wording to «computed before, persisted with the locked artifacts».

verdict.reasoning: SEPARATE BLOCKING DEFECT FOUND WHILE VERIFYING THIS ITEM (it does not change L1-2's severity). runner._progress (runner.py:185-189) calls pair.curve(). PairedCandidate.curve() (train.py:447-450) runs CandidateCurve.validate(), which raises ValueError('incomplete candidate curve') whenever the last point's exposure differs from the approved horizon (selection.py:103-104). That is the case at every checkpoint before the horizon, starting with the step-zero point. runner.py:294 and :299 pass on_checkpoint=_progress to every controls and real-selection stage, which are the 11 search jobs (CV_MULTIPLICITY sums to 11, resources.py:14). Each one therefore crashes right after the step-zero evaluation of both folds. It writes a technical_failure receipt (runner.py:383-389), and the existing-receipt guard (runner.py:216) then refuses to rerun that logical ID. The chain stops at the first neural controls job, a few GPU-minutes in, and needs a code fix plus a new plan and review. This is blocking under the stated criterion: it makes a job fail. The 204 new tests missed it because test_pose_temponet_runner.py:59-63 replaces workflow.run_selection with a fake that ignores on_checkpoint, and the train and workflow tests run searches with on_checkpoint=None. Minimal fix, runtime change, logging only, no numerical effect: in _progress, read pair.points directly instead of calling pair.curve(), e.g. `if pair.points: print(json.dumps({"event": "selection_checkpoint", "lr": pair.lr, "point": _plain(asdict(pair.points[-1]))}, allow_nan=False), flush=True)`. Add a CPU test that runs T._run_search with the test recipe and on_checkpoint=runner._progress. On L1-2 itself, confirmed by the code. Trajectory.initial_sha256 is computed at construction (train.py:232) and checked across LRs (train.py:547-550). It is persisted only in the selection report (train.py:563), inside Trajectory.state() payloads (train.py:324), and in the refit manifest (workflow.py:404). All of these are written by runner._save_results after the stage completes (runner.py:302). Failure receipts carry only allocation, elapsed time and error. findings.title: A failed pooled closed-form gate is recorded as technical_failure inside the six GPU control jobs
findings.claim: If both folds calibrate but the pooled closed-form qualification fails (linear ridge recovers less than 90%, or the temporal clean-LS band is outside [0.06, 0.10]), the state should be controllo_non_diagnostico. Instead `_calibrations` raises a plain ValueError through P.require, so run_stage writes status technical_failure. Nobody evaluates the pooled gate before the GPU stage, so all six GPU control jobs are allocated just to fail at start. The combined gate (recoveries and band per split) is never saved as an artifact. findings.claim: P §4.4 defines `controllo_non_diagnostico` as a prespecified gate outcome that stops the chain before the neural fits. The P §4.5 list of technical failures does not include it. The runner checks this outcome with `P.require(controls.combine_reference_folds(values)["status"] == "diagnostic", "closed-form controls are not diagnostic")`, which raises a ValueError, not GateNotPassed. Line 388 therefore maps it to status `technical_failure`. The check runs for the first time inside the six `controls` GPU jobs: the two `wls_calibration` jobs only test their own fold's `calibrated` status, and no stage between them evaluates the combined fold0/fold1/pooled gate. The combined gate dict, with linear_gate and temporal_gate and the margins that failed, is never written.
findings.evidence: Scratch test /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-simonebenatti-dev-wearusfm/d9aa6af4-72b7-4d2a-8229-4444e8ca2c8f/scratchpad/poseheads/agents/lens5/test_final_glue.py::test_non_diagnostic_closed_form_is_labelled uses the existing runner fixture. It completes both calibrations, then monkeypatches combine_reference_folds to return control_non_diagnostic. Output for each of the six jobs, for example ('TCNH-controls-linear-L0-20261119', 1 GPU, 'technical_failure', 'ValueError', 'closed-form controls are not diagnostic', artifacts=[]), with the same result for linear MLP/TCN_post and temporal L0/MLP/TCN_post. Also: `isinstance(ValueError(...), runner.GateNotPassed)` is False. By contrast, `control_non_calibrated` correctly raises GateNotPassed and gives `gate_failed` (runner.py:285-286).
findings.failure_scenario: Real calibrations both reach status `calibrated`, but the pooled linear 90% margin or the temporal [6%,10%] band fails. SLURM releases all six control GPU jobs through afterok. Each one allocates an A100, verifies receipts, loads the calibration states and fails. Result: six `technical_failure` receipts, each with only the error string and no saved gate values. P §4.5 says a technical failure should be diagnosed before a new decision. This outcome is a defined scientific gate result, so the operator is misdirected, and the receipts lack the evidence of why the control was non-diagnostic. A few GPU allocations are also spent on a gate that can be computed on CPU.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_calibrations`, or at the start of the controls stage, compute `combine_reference_folds` once and save it as an artifact (for example closed_form_gate.json). If its status is not "diagnostic", raise `GateNotPassed("control_non_diagnostic")`. Make the same change at workflow.py:165 for consistency. Better still, evaluate the combined gate in a CPU stage or at the end of the second calibration so that no GPU job is released, if the graph can change without a new design decision.

verdict.reasoning: The code supports the finding. `_calibrations` (runner.py:98-103) uses P.require, which raises a plain ValueError (provenance.py:65-67). `run_stage` then labels it technical_failure (runner.py:388). The wls_calibration branch (runner.py:271-286) tests only its own fold's `calibrated` status. Both calibration jobs depend only on the benchmarks, so they run in parallel and neither can see the other fold. The graph (execution.py:48-55) places the six 1-GPU controls jobs directly after the two calibrations. The combined fold0/fold1/pooled gate is therefore evaluated for the first time inside each GPU controls job, and the failure receipt carries no gate dict. The spec treats this outcome as a gate state, not a technical failure: J failure_states lists `controllo_non_diagnostico` separately from `technical_failure`; J linear.closed_form_diagnostic.failure says 'control_non_diagnostic before neural fits'; P §4.5's technical_failure list does not include it. The execution doc says 'Il controller distingue gate_failed da technical_failure'. Its table makes 'entrambe le calibrazioni e gate dei riferimenti' the condition before submitting the controls, yet no stage or CLI command produces that gate. A further point supports the finding: workflow.qualify_controls:336-338 has a path that turns a non-diagnostic result into a recordable gate dict (positive_gate.json), followed by GateNotPassed at runner.py:239-243. That path is unreachable, because `_calibrations` raises first at runner.py:236. Several factors keep the severity below blocking. The chain still stops before any neural fit, and no wrong result is admitted. The error string ('closed-form controls are not diagnostic') states the cause. The inputs to the gate (outer_reference_statistics) are kept in each calibration.json, so the gate can be recomputed. The GPU spend is six short allocations. This is a real defect with limited consequence, so important is the right severity.

findings.title: The necessary condition point E_dyn <= 0.7630564046643697 is neither checked explicitly nor recorded in the candidacy
findings.claim: J evaluation.candidate.trained_head_point_threshold_necessary, P §5 and the P §10 table make `point E_dyn <= 0.7630564046643697` an explicit necessary condition. `candidacy()` checks only common gates, comparator alarms, the BENEFIT labels on 1/4/5, the vetoes on 2/3 and evaluability. The threshold is implied only through the contrast-5 condition gain>=2, where E_ref is the trained-head E_dyn recomputed from per-user sums. That value differs from 0.7786289843513977 because of summation order, by a few ulp. R-1 tolerates up to 1e-12. The threshold appears nowhere in the code, plan or tests (grep for 7630564 returns nothing).
findings.evidence: Snippet: with ref=0.7786289843513977 the two conditions are equivalent at float precision: E=0.7630564046643697 gives gain 2.0000000000000013 (passes), and the next float 0.7630564046643699 gives 1.9999999999999871 (fails). With ref=np.nextafter(ref,1)=0.7786289843513978, E=0.7630564046643699 gives gain>=2 True, although it is above the explicit threshold. A reference that passes R-1 but is off by up to 1e-12 widens this window to about 1e-12.
findings.failure_scenario: Practically negligible. A pooled TCN E_dyn inside the ulp to 1e-12 window above 0.7630564046643697 would be declared a candidate although the prespecified necessary condition fails. Separately, the published candidacy never shows that this condition was checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the conjunct `_points(averaged["TCN_post"]["dynamic"])["E_dyn"] <= 0.7630564046643697` to `candidate`. Pass the point into candidacy() and record the value and the threshold in the output, for example `trained_head_point_threshold_passed`.

verdict.reasoning: `candidacy()` (report.py:190-196) has no conjunct for the frozen point threshold. The J field `candidate.trained_head_point_threshold_necessary` (proposal.json:70) is not used anywhere in scripts/, tests or the plan; grep for 7630564 matches only the spec files. The threshold is enforced only implicitly, through contrast 5 (gain>=2). That contrast uses E_ref recomputed from the historical predictions, which R-1 holds to within 1e-12 of 0.7786289843513977 (metrics.py:185). The literal threshold and the code's decision can therefore disagree inside a window of at most about 1e-12. In mitigation, P §5's 'se e solo se' rule (gates, admitted comparators, 1/4/5 BENEFIT, no 2/3 HARM) is implemented exactly, and the threshold is a derived restatement (0.98*0.7786289843513977 rounds to exactly 0.7630564046643697). The practical effect is nil; the real gap is that the P §10 'necessario' condition is neither checked nor recorded. Minor is right.
verdict.evidence: Snippet output. 0.98*ref = 0.7630564046643697 (the exact product rounds to the same double). With ref=0.7786289843513977: gain(thr)=2.0000000000000013, while the next double, 0.7630564046643699, gives 1.9999999999999871 and fails. With ref one ulp higher: gain(0.7630564046643699)=2.0000000000000013 and passes, although it is above the literal threshold. With ref+1e-12, the maximum R-1 tolerance: 8826 doubles above the threshold, up to delta 9.8e-13, still pass gain>=2. Suggested fix (runtime): add the conjunct and record `trained_head_point_threshold_passed` with the value in the candidacy output.

findings.title: The second R-1 parity check, run before the contrasts, leaves no record in the metrics receipt or report
findings.claim: P §8 and J require R-1 'before neural fits and again before contrasts'. The metrics stage runs `parity = metrics.historical_reference_gate(...)` followed by `P.require(parity["passed"], ...)`, but `parity` is discarded. The receipt's gates.historical_R1 is copied from the preflight (line 227), and receipt details hold only allocation and elapsed_seconds.
findings.evidence: Scratch smoke test test_final_glue.py::test_final_stage_glue runs locked_inference, metrics and collection through the real runner glue. It prints `details keys ['allocation', 'elapsed_seconds']` for the completed metrics receipt. The report's common_gates.historical_R1 is the preflight value.
findings.failure_scenario: The published evidence cannot show that the pre-contrast parity ran, or which values and counts it observed. A reviewer of the final receipts has to trust the code path. If R-1 fails, the stage does stop with technical_failure, so the results themselves are not wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the result, for example `details["historical_R1_before_contrasts"] = parity`, or add it to report.json next to common_gates.

verdict.reasoning: In the metrics stage (runner.py:340-341), `parity = metrics.historical_reference_gate(...)` is followed by `P.require(parity["passed"], ...)`, and `parity` is then discarded. On failure, metrics.historical_reference_gate raises itself, so the P.require is redundant. On success it returns observed values and counts, but none of them are stored. The receipt's gates.historical_R1 (runner.py:226-228) and the report's common_gates both copy the preflight result. The re-check does run and stops the chain on failure, so results are not affected. Part of the evidence can be rebuilt: report.json `references` holds the recomputed historical E_dyn points, and `paired_user_accumulators` holds the per-user counts from the same validation cache. Missing are the explicit pass record, the tolerance, n_selected_windows (8329) and the crop-identity check. This is a transparency gap, so minor is right.
verdict.evidence: The scratch run of test_final_stage_glue (my copy, passed) printed `metrics receipt status completed gates ['calibration', 'closed_references', 'historical_R1', 'inference_locked', 'integrity', 'positive_controls', 'refits_locked', 'resources', 'selection_locked']` and `details keys ['allocation', 'elapsed_seconds']`. The preflight does keep its full R-1 dict (provenance.py:462, `"historical_R1":result`). Suggested fix (runtime): `details["historical_R1_before_contrasts"] = parity`.

findings.title: al_bordo_MC skips CI endpoints of exactly 1.9 or 2.1 because of binary floating point, although the rule is inclusive
findings.claim: `monte_carlo_border` uses `abs(float(x)-threshold) <= .1`. The spec reads 'within 0.1 pp of 0 or 2', which is inclusive. At 0 the endpoint 0.1 is flagged. At 2, abs(1.9-2.0)=0.10000000000000009 > 0.1, so the decimal boundaries 1.9 and 2.1 are not flagged.
findings.evidence: Scratch check output: [0.1,3] True; [-0.1,3] True; [1.9,5] False; [2.1,5] False; [0.2,1.95] True. The committed test uses 1.91 and 2.11 and does not cover the exact boundary.
findings.failure_scenario: Only a CI endpoint within about one ulp of 1.9 or 2.1 is affected: the flag is missing for it and the label is unchanged. The practical probability is negligible. The defect is the asymmetry with the 0 threshold.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare with a small absolute tolerance, for example `abs(x-t) <= 0.1 + 1e-12`, and add exact-boundary cases (1.9, 2.1, 0.1, -0.1) to the test.

verdict.reasoning: The claimed defect comes from reading decimal literals, not from the code. The decimal numbers 1.9 and 2.1 cannot be represented. The double nearest 1.9 is 1.8999999999999999112, which lies 0.1000000000000000888 from 2 in exact arithmetic, so it is genuinely outside an inclusive 0.1 band. For x in [1,4], `2-x` is exact (Sterbenz lemma), so `abs(x-2)` is the exact distance. The code compares it with float(0.1) = 0.1+5.55e-18, so it flags every double whose exact distance to 2 is at most 0.1, plus a 5.55e-18 margin on the inclusive side. The very next double after 1.9 (1.9000000000000001, distance 0.09999999999999987) is flagged. At threshold 0 the double 0.1 is flagged, although its exact value is 5.55e-18 beyond 0.1. The only deviation anywhere is therefore a negligible over-inclusion, never a missed endpoint. No computed CI endpoint truly within 0.1 pp of 2 escapes the flag. The suggested +1e-12 tolerance would instead flag endpoints that are genuinely outside the band. At most there is a cosmetic quirk: an endpoint whose shortest form prints as '1.9' is not flagged. That is not a defect, so 'minor' overstates it.
verdict.evidence: Fractions check: 1.9 vs 2 gives computed 0.10000000000000009, exact distance within 0.1 False, code False. 2.1 vs 2 gives the same. 0.1 vs 0 gives exact distance within 0.1 False, within float(0.1) True, code True. The dense neighbourhood check: 1.9 has exact distance 0.10000000000000009 and is not flagged; 1.9000000000000001 has exact distance 0.09999999999999987, within 0.1 True, code True; 1.9000000000000004 and 1.9000000000000006 are also flagged. float(0.1)-0.1 = 5.55e-18. Code: report.py:49-51 `abs(float(x)-threshold) <= .1`.
